formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: marketValue = shares × price × multiplier, unrounded; 0 shares → $0; no price or unknown count → unknown. 5 of 5 cases agree.

formula_checks.name: unrealizedGain
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Correct on the stated finite, valid-input domain. This is a specification judgment; ingestion, actual UI and app execution are not provided.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: In the working tree (2026-10-20) unrealizedGain counts only the purchases whose price paid is on record (paidOnRecord): value of those units − what was paid for them. The card's words ("market value − cost") describe HEAD; they need updating once that work lands. 5 of 5 cases agree on both.
formula_checks.plain_example: 10 sh at $100 + a 0-share lot with no price, price $90: −$100.

formula_checks.name: capGains
formula_checks.reviewer_why: A known zero basis is treated as missing, contradicting costBasis and unknownFigure. Undated lots are asserted short-term without evidence. Generic option tax classification is oversimplified.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: capGains reads each lot's date with new Date(purchase_date): a null date is 1 Jan 1970 (long-term), a blank date is unreadable and goes to short-term. A $0 price paid is "not on record" in the working tree (left out and counted). The Holding page draws the IF YOU SOLD TODAY split for any priced holding, whatever the account (HoldingDetailScreen.tsx, `cg && !closed`).
formula_checks.plain_example: 3.25 mini-option contracts bought at $2.37 with no date, now $4.13: "Gain — long-term +$57" (null date) or "short-term +$57" (blank date); the honest answer is +$57 with the holding period not on record.

parts.point: Known zero basis treated as missing
parts.see: case "Three lots and known zero adjusted basis"
case "Unknown date is not short-term evidence"; plus a null date read as 1970 → long-term
the split is shown in IRAs, 401(k)s and Roth accounts, where neither rate applies; its labels state the holding period ("held over 1 yr"), not a tax

formula_checks.name: totalROI
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Aggregate unrealized gain / aggregate cost is not time-weighted for staggered purchases and excludes distributions. The owner requires every return to be TWR.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: totalROI = gain ÷ what was paid, over the purchases whose price paid is on record. Shown only as the percent beside "Change since purchase" on the Holding page; never labelled "return". The window return of a holding bought inside the window is returnSincePurchases (time-weighted).
governing_decisions: precision standard § return on cost (with DEC-1669)
formula_checks.plain_example: 10 at $100 then 10 at $110, now $121: Change since purchase +$320 (+15.24%) — right for that label; the window return is a separate figure.
formula_checks.note: Fix the card's wording ("Total return since purchase" → "return on what was paid"); no code change.

formula_checks.name: startDateFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Since exists on screens but is not a Period value and needs a caller-supplied start. Human labels versus canonical keys and invalid now are not settled.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: startDateFor reads one table of window names (WINDOW_MONTHS) and refuses any other, "SINCE" included (DEC-4640); the screens hand Since's first day to buildPerformance (windowStartKey: the day after the record's first day). An invalid `now` gives an Invalid Date, not nothing — unreachable: every caller passes the clock or a checked day.
formula_checks.plain_example: Record from 4 May 2026: Since opens 5 May, measured from the 4 May close.

formula_checks.name: latestClose
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Latest date can be future or malformed, and duplicate-date conflicting prices have no rule.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: latestClose reads the close on the latest valid date, in any order, skipping unreadable dates; for two closes on one date it takes the one listed later. It has no `now`: capping at today belongs to its callers (see MK-PF-F-010, F-011).
formula_checks.plain_example: Two 20 Sep closes, $91.43 then $97.31: 10 shares are worth $973.10 (later one) or $914.30 (earlier one).
formula_checks.recommendation: Keep the later-listed close (the feed lists in time order, so it is the newer quote) and say so on the card.

formula_checks.name: periodReturn
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Latest close is not capped at now. Short-history fallback contradicts periodReturnParts; exact two-year exponent disagrees with orchestrator days/365 annualization.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: periodReturnParts ends at latestClose, not at today, so a close dated after today is used. Short history: one reader, closeAsOf, falls back to the first price (DEC-4641) — no divergence in the code (that part of the verdict reads the packet's prose). 2Y yearly rate: exponent 1/2 when prices reach back, else days ÷ 365.25; thePerformance uses window days ÷ 365 with both edge days counted (731 for an ordinary 2Y).
formula_checks.plain_example: Future close: +17.00% instead of +9.93%. Annualising: one +21.00% two-year move reads +10.00% a year on the holding row and +9.99% a year on the Performance total.

parts.point: Latest close not capped at now
Short-history fallback contradicts the parts reader
parts.why: the code has one reader (closeAsOf with the first-price fallback, DEC-4641); case "Short history of five months" agrees

parts.example: same +21.00% over 13 Oct 2024 → 13 Oct 2026: holding row +10.00% a year, Performance total +9.99% a year (731 days)

formula_checks.name: periodReturnSince
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Now is handed in but latest close ignores it; a future explicit start can be priced before the start, and elapsed spans over one year are never annualized here.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: periodReturnSince ignores `now`: it ends at the latest close and a start after today returns +0.00%; an unreadable start date falls back to the first close. Never made yearly — including a holding bought more than a year back viewed under 2Y ("Your return since purchase").
formula_checks.plain_example: Start 1 Nov 2026, today 13 Oct 2026: +0.00% instead of no figure. Bought 13 Apr 2025, viewed under 2Y: "+21.00%" over 18 months, no "a year" (about +13.54% a year by 365 ÷ days).

parts.point: Spans over a year never annualised here
parts.why: DEC-0237 makes a window longer than a year a yearly rate; the v17 exception covers the record's Since, not a purchase cap

formula_checks.name: earliestPurchaseDate
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Dated zero-share or future lots can cap performance before the holding actually existed; partial missing dates produce false certainty.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: earliestPurchaseDate takes the earliest valid date of ANY lot — a lot of 0 shares or a date after today included — and ignores undated lots.
formula_checks.plain_example: A 0-share lot dated 11 Mar 2024 before real purchases from 19 May 2026: the row is measured over the whole year (+21.64%) instead of since the first real purchase (+17.00%).

parts.point: Zero-share lot caps before the holding existed

parts.see: case "One missing date before known dates is possible"

formula_checks.name: benchmarkTicker
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Recognized wrapper kinds select AOR despite a broker-classified stock or bond; explicit unknown class/kind strings fall back to SPY. The classification authority needs to be settled.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: benchmarkTicker lets a class decide only when the person set it, or no kind names a yardstick; otherwise the kind's table entry wins — wrapper kinds (401k, IRA, Roth, HSA, 529) map to AOR. It does not read the class reader (holdingClassOf), which since 2026-10-20 follows the class the broker sends. A kind or class with no yardstick of its own → SPY.
formula_checks.plain_example: A bond fund in a 401(k), broker says bond: Net worth files it under Bonds & CDs; its yardstick is AOR (60/40), not AGG.

parts.point: Wrapper kind beats a broker-classified bond
Unknown kind/class strings fall back to SPY
parts.example: an Alternatives holding (class other, no kind) is set beside the S&P 500

formula_checks.name: buildPerformance
formula_checks.reviewer_why: ReturnSincePurchases values old shares at the purchase-day close before adding the morning purchase, contrary to DEC-4439; undated lots are moved to an invented first day. Zero-purchase caps and short-history parts also diverge.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: buildPerformance: a holding bought inside the window is time-weighted from its purchases by returnSincePurchases, which ends each piece at the purchase DAY's close (money counted as arriving at the end of the day). Undated lots are placed on the first dated day. Dollar facts (value, what was paid, gain, return on what was paid) are separate fields from the window return.
formula_checks.plain_example: 10 bought 1 Sep at $100, 10 bought 2 Sep at $110, closes $100 / $121 / $121: +26.76% shown, +15.24% by DEC-4439.

parts.point: Purchase placed after the day's growth (DEC-4439)
Undated lots moved to an invented first day

needs_a_ruling.item: A stored $0 price paid: a real $0, or a blank?
needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Holding page: Total paid, Change since purchase, IF YOU SOLD TODAY; Performance row what was paid and gain.
needs_a_ruling.what_changes: 7.25 sh at $83.17 (2024), 3.125 at $91.43 (2026), 2.5 at $0 (2024); price $97.31. Real $0: long-term +$346, short-term +$18, total +$364, Total paid $889 for 12.875 shares. Blank (working tree): long-term +$103, short-term +$18, total +$121 on 10.375 of 12.875 shares, with a line naming the 2.5 shares.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Since 2026-10-20 a blank is stored as nothing, so treat a $0 typed from now on as real; $0 saved before cannot be told apart. Whatever is chosen, costBasis must read it the same way (Plan's taxable share reads costBasis).

needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Holding price and value on Performance and the Holding page, and every return ending that day.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Keep the later-listed close (the newer quote).

needs_a_ruling.item: A holding with one undated and one dated purchase
needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Performance holding row and Holding page window return and "Versus the market".
needs_a_ruling.what_changes: 10 sh (no date, paid $80) + 7 bought 19 May 2026 at $83.17; $97.31 today; 1Y. Today: "since purchase" +19.68% vs market +5.77% from 19 May. Treated as held all year: +21.64% vs market +10.00%. Refused: no figure, a line names the 10 undated shares.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Ask the ledger's first buy first; otherwise treat it like a holding with no dated purchase (tenet 4).

needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Performance 2Y: a holding row's yearly rate beside the total's yearly rate.
needs_a_ruling.what_changes: Same +21.00% over 13 Oct 2024 → 13 Oct 2026: holding row +10.00% a year (exponent 1/2); Performance total +9.99% a year (731 days ÷ 365).
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Calendar years: an exact 2Y window is 2 years, as an exact 1Y is already read as a year on the calendar; 365 ÷ days only for spans that are not whole calendar years.

needs_a_ruling.item: A holding bought more than a year back, under the 2Y chip
needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Holding page "Your return since purchase"; Performance 2Y holding row.
needs_a_ruling.what_changes: Bought 13 Apr 2025 at $100, $121 today: shown +21.00% (18 months' total, no "a year"); as a yearly rate it would be +13.54% a year with +21.00% beside it.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Show it like the 2Y figure (yearly rate, total beside), per DEC-0237; the Since exception is for the record's Since only.

needs_a_ruling.item: The long-term / short-term split inside tax-free accounts
needs_a_ruling.where_on_screen: Holding page IF YOU SOLD TODAY, for a holding in an IRA, 401(k), Roth or HSA.
needs_a_ruling.what_changes: 10 shares bought 2024 at $100, $120 today, in a Roth IRA: shows "Gain — long-term (held over 1 yr) +$200", though no capital-gains rate applies there.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Hide the card for tax-advantaged accounts, or say the split is the holding period only.
